metaTitle: Interior Renovation Contractors in Ontario: A Guide
metaDescription: How to vet an interior renovation contractor in Ontario, from permits and subtrade coordination to realistic costs and questions worth asking first.
intro: Interior renovations range from a single room refresh to a full-home reconfiguration, and the scope changes who you need to hire and how permits apply. A good general contractor coordinates every subtrade and keeps the project on a realistic schedule.
whatToLookFor: A general contractor with a defined process for coordinating subtrades
Experience with projects of a similar scope and age of home
Knowledge of when a building permit is required for structural changes
A detailed written scope of work, not just a verbal outline
References from recent, comparable renovation projects
typicalCostNotes: Interior renovation costs vary enormously by scope, from a cosmetic refresh to structural changes involving walls, plumbing or electrical, so most jobs are genuinely quoted per project. Older homes often carry extra cost for unexpected issues found once walls are opened, and permit and design fees can add to a structural project. Ask for a contingency allowance built into the estimate, since it is common for even a well-planned renovation to encounter something unexpected once demolition starts.
questionsToAsk: Will this project require a building permit, and who pulls it?
How do you sequence and supervise subtrades on site?
What is included in the written scope, and what is an allowance?
How do you handle changes or surprises found once work begins?
Can I see a similar completed project or speak with that client?
redFlags: No written scope of work or itemized estimate
Dismissing the need for a permit on structural changes
A large upfront deposit before any material is ordered
